newsitem.title: INDIA: India's 96/97 crude oil output seen at 36.31 mln t.
newsitem.headline: India's 96/97 crude oil output seen at 36.31 mln t.

text.p: India's crude oil production is expected to reach a level of 36.31 million tonnes in 1996/97 (April-March), the independent Centre for Monitoring Indian Economy (CMIE) said.
This will represent a marginal five percent rise over the 1995/96 figure, CMIE said an energy sector review received by Reuters on Friday.
The estimate for 1996/97 includes 0.5 million tonnes of production by private and joint venture firms, it said.

The 1996/97 projections fall below the government's 37.45 million tonnes target for 1995/96, CMIE said. It attributed the fall to lowering of production targets for Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC), the state-run firm that accounts for 90 percent of India's oil production.

"The petroleum ministry has attributed the projected fall to reduction in anticipated production from the major fields in Bombay High and Neelam and subdued activities in enhanced oil recovery programme," the CMIE survey said.

During 1995/96, India imported 27.35 million tonnes of crude oil, the report said. "Though imports during 1995/96 were similar in physical terms, they were higher by 12 percent in value terms (over the year ago period)," it said.
It said the petroleum ministry estimated total crude oil requirement in 1996/97 at 61.66 million tonnes. The domestic production would be supplemented by import of 26.62 million tonnes.

"The value of import during 1996/97 is estimated at $3.4 billion, both under term contract and spot purchases. Of these, 19.5 million tonnes would be against term contracts and the balance from open market, CMIE said.
Five countries -- Saudi Arabia, UAE, Kuwait, Nigeria and Iran -- accounted for 96 percent of the total crude oil imported during 1995/96, CMIE said.
Among them, Saudi Arabia has been the major source, accounting for 26 percent of oil imports.
